value:
DECIDED 2026-06-09: MCP stays. Don't re-litigate from token economics — after the #124-#127 diet the surface delta is noise, and the dominant cost (bootstrap content) is identical on both surfaces; the token lever is store discipline, not transport.

THE REAL LEDGER: MCP is push (auto-injected via .mcp.json — the adoption channel for users who never curate CLAUDE.md), serves no-shell surfaces (Claude Desktop/claude.ai/IDE-lite — the mirror image of the ban-MCP cohort that justified #117), is safer for writes (JSON params vs shell-quoting KB-sized multi-line seeds), and is a commercial checkbox. CLI serves the MCP-banned cohort and wins filterable analytical reads via pipes. The exclusions don't overlap — the DUAL-SURFACE design is the moat; neither side is redundant.

EVIDENCE (all-time telemetry at decision): 944/1266 calls (75%) via MCP across 63 multi-call agent sessions (~15 calls each); 322 CLI calls are one-shot processes (parity pending #119). Both surfaces fully instrumented (src:cli/mcp in audit+telemetry).

COSTS ACCEPTED: MCP SDK dep tree (fast-uri advisory arrived through it) + the long-lived-process bug class (all 3 historical freezes were MCP-only, see [[context.mcpServerFreezeDiagnosis]]).

KILL CRITERIA (revisit only on these): usage collapses to shell-capable agents only; SDK maintenance tax spikes again; a successor standard displaces MCP. AFTER full parity (#119 + #124-#127): soften generated guidance from "prefer MCP" to "same store, either surface; pipe the CLI when you'd filter." See [[context.surfaceTokenEconomics]], [[project.cliAgentParity]].
